runtime_prompt_en:
Use the first attached image as the source photograph for this local support-contact edit. Use the second attached portrait to retain the face and hair appearance. Preserve the source image's continuous forearm-to-metal join, drum-wrap contact, brake grip, archival glass plates, lighting and suspended dust. A photographic horror scene presents a fictional adult woman caught in a complex horror situation. Preserve the supplied portrait's face and hair appearance: the soft oval facial outline, round dark brown eyes, small defined nose, naturally pink lips, short dark bob and separated fine fringe remain recognizable. Her softly parted lips and warm facial detail keep an intimate human presence against the machine. In an underground archive lift machinery room, she is trying to keep a wooden tray of glass photographic plates from slipping into a gate edge as the loaded lift stalls halfway between landings. She wears a faded charcoal work shirt with both sleeves rolled above the elbows and plain dark trousers. Her hips brace against a square guardrail. At pelvis height, her machine-side clothed hip presses firmly into the flat side of a fixed square-section steel guardrail. The trouser cloth has a short visibly flattened contact patch against the rail, with compressed fabric folds fanning outward from that contact. The same rail leads to a rigid support post descending toward the floor, visibly carrying the counterforce against the pulling belt. This hip-to-rail contact stays plainly exposed below the elbow and tissue-metal transition, with a clear air gap between the rail and the bronze belt. Her right arm remains in the established brake action: her right hand grips the spring-loaded brake lever close to her waist, and her left upper arm leads through one human elbow toward the exposed winding drum. Warm skin creases along the exposed left forearm progressively turn into ridged living bronze; the same fine capillary paths cross the sealed continuous transition and become grooves in a flattened bronze tendon-belt. At her exposed forearm, organic tissue and metal meet at one shared junction: the skin's capillary tracery becomes bronze grooves within the same surface. Her left wrist and hand have become this single belt, which continues from the forearm in one uninterrupted strip and winds tightly around the drum. Its taut span visibly transmits the lift's load back into her arm. Across that unbroken forearm-to-belt conversion, both structures continue through the join under the same pulling tension. A floor-mounted worm gear sits below the drum; the working brake tooth has slipped across its wheel, leaving a fresh bright scuff beside the dull worn track, and her right-hand lever is holding it at the edge of the next tooth. Behind and beside the drum, the tray leans on the tilted lift deck and one glass plate projects over the near gate lip; the connected steel lift cable stays under tension. Her head turns toward the taut belt, with both eyes and the fringe clearly exposed. The progressive organic-to-metal junction is the first focal point, the recognizable face is second, and the threatened glass plate and brake contact complete the cause and consequence. Pale mineral-green task light rakes across the bronze ridges, while a low warm emergency lamp keeps skin, fine hairs and glass edges legible. Suspended paper dust brightens only within the narrow green worklamp beam, while the lift rails and tray beyond the illuminated haze keep crisp recognizable edges. Make a vertical environmental portrait from knees upward, from a chest-height three-quarter front viewpoint on her left side; place face, full human elbow, transformation, taut span and drum contact within the same clear depth plane, with the brake hand and lift tray also readable. Moderate depth of field, natural perspective, restrained film grain and consistent specular reflections give this impossible conversion the material weight of a photographed event.

Avoid: 3d render look, awkward animal anatomy, body distortion, broken facial features, broken window geometry, cartoon style, cgi look, digital illustration, distorted fingers, excessive hdr, fake-looking background, flat collage look, illustration look, impossible perspective, inaccurate reflections, inconsistent shadows, low resolution, obvious cutout edges, over-processed retouching, overly smooth fur, plastic-looking food texture, plastic-looking skin, unmatched lighting, unrealistic hands, unrealistic steam, warped product geometry, warped walls
